newsitem.title: INDIA: Miss World given go-ahead, suicide threat renewed.
newsitem.headline: Miss World given go-ahead, suicide threat renewed.

text.p: An Indian woman renewed her threat to burn herself to death in protest against the Miss World beauty contest after a court on Tuesday said the pagent could proceed in the southern city of Bangalore.
A man in Madurai, 432 kilometres (270 miles) from Bangalore in neighbouring Tamil Nadu state, burned himself to death last week in protest against the pagent.

"My protests will be peaceful. By burning myself I will not be disrupting the show. We will go-ahead with our earlier plan," Kina Narayana Shashikala, leader of the Mahila Jagran Samiti (Forum for Awakening Women) told Reuters after a court rejected the group's petition to block the pagent.
The traditionalist group had held its threat of self-immolation in abeyance until the court decision was known.
"We declined to ban the show," R.P. Sethi, chief justice of the Karnataka High Court, told a packed courtroom. "The state government should not prevent peaceful protests."
Shashikala has said several of her followers will join the 20,000 people expected to attend the Miss World crowning ceremony on November 23 and take cyanide pills before setting themselves ablaze.
People attending events at the Miss World gala have been frisked by police, who confiscated cigarette lighters and bags.
Now, in addition to the de facto ban on smoking, the court on Tuesday told pagent organisers that no alcohol should be served at the Chinnaswamy cricket stadium where the open air show is being held.
The pagent finale is expected to be seen by an estimated two billion television viewers worldwide.

A protester of the Michael Jackson concert in Bombay in late October also threatened to burn himself but was detained by police before he could commit suicide. Under Indian law, police can take people into custody as a preventive measure.
